t: Capability indexing of the tool registry (foundational)
title: Capability indexing of the tool registry (foundational)
description: Signature original: Every registered tool is indexed by its declared capabilities: verbs it performs, data types it consumes and produces, and constraints it honors. The index is built once at registration and updated on every registry change. Good indexing makes matching a lookup problem instead of a search problem. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example. Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH).
provenance: Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH) for Capability-to-Tool Matcher, 2026-10-21.

title: Requirement parsing from task text (foundational)
description: Signature original: The task description is parsed into a requirement frame: the action verb, input and output types, and hard constraints like 'offline only'. Parsing uses keyword patterns over a controlled vocabulary, which keeps it predictable. The frame is what gets matched, never the raw prose. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example. Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH).
demo:
# Signature-authored original (JAH).
import re
task = 'hash these bytes offline and verify the digest'
frame = {'verb': 'hash', 'io': ('bytes', 'digest'), 'offline': bool(re.search(r'offline', task))}
print('requirement frame:', frame)
provenance: Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH) for Capability-to-Tool Matcher, 2026-10-21.

title: Match scoring with constraint veto (foundational)
description: Signature original: Candidate tools are scored by capability overlap with the requirement frame, but any violated hard constraint vetoes the candidate outright. A tool that matches perfectly but needs network access loses to an offline-capable partial match when the task demands offline. Vetoes keep the matcher honest about requirements. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example. Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH).
demo:
# Signature-authored original (JAH).
cands = [('hash-tool', 0.95, True), ('cloud-hash', 1.0, False)]  # (tool, score, offline_ok)
need_offline = True
viable = [(t, s) for t, s, off in cands if not (need_offline and not off)]
print('viable:', viable)
provenance: Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH) for Capability-to-Tool Matcher, 2026-10-21.

t: Fallback chaining when no single tool fits (foundational)
title: Fallback chaining when no single tool fits (foundational)
description: Signature original: When no single tool covers the whole task, the matcher chains tools by matching one's output type to the next one's input type, like the workflow composer's smaller cousin. Chains are ranked by total score minus a per-hop penalty, so shorter chains win ties. The chain ships as an ordered tool list with the handoff types explicit. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example. Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH).
demo:
# Signature-authored original (JAH).
tools = {'a': ('docs', 'index'), 'b': ('index', 'hits')}
chain = ['a', 'b'] if tools['a'][1] == tools['b'][0] else []
print('fallback chain:', ' -> '.join(chain) if chain else 'none found')
provenance: Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH) for Capability-to-Tool Matcher, 2026-10-21.

title: Match explanation for the user (foundational)
description: Signature original: The chosen tool or chain is presented with its explanation: which capabilities matched, which constraints were honored, and what the fallbacks were. Explanations let users sanity-check the match instead of trusting a black box. A match the user cannot understand is a match they cannot trust. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example. Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH).
demo:
# Signature-authored original (JAH).
print('matched: hash-tool | capabilities: hash, verify | constraints honored: offline | runner-up: cloud-hash (vetoed: needs network)')
provenance: Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH) for Capability-to-Tool Matcher, 2026-10-21.
